I'll start by reading the docs and looking at the data.

I need the truncated middle of the rules.

That call was malformed. I'll simplify the repeated-time logic in `local_to_epoch` first.

I wrote `/app/bin/payroll.py`, ran it on `/app/data`, and saved the result as `/app/out/payroll.json`. `python3 /app/tools/check_payroll.py` reports "OK: every value matches the approved figures." That covers all 150 employees on every field, plus the exception counts and totals.

The script uses only the standard library and takes its rules from the docs. It reads gzip-compressed files whatever their names, and reads every file under each site's export folder. It handles all seven export formats, including the repeated headers, schema switches and clock offsets they describe. The run took about 1.3 seconds.

`/app/STATUS.json` is written with status "success".

I tested it only on this period's data. The other periods' exports may hit edge cases this one doesn't. One example is an employee with a shift but no rate on or before the shift's workday. The docs don't say what to do there, so the script uses the employee's earliest rate.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -type f | head -100; cat docs/payroll-rules.md docs/exports.md docs/output.md

cd /app; ls data | head; ls data/corrections | head -30; ls data/exports; cat data/sites.csv data/period.json; head -5 data/employees.csv data/rates.csv; cat tools/check_payroll.py | head -60; ls bin out

cd /app/data; for s in harbor-point southbank ridgeline lakeshore kiln marrow summit northgate tarai; do echo "=== $s"; ls exports/$s | wc -l; f=$(ls exports/$s | head -3 | tail -1); file exports/$s/$f; head -c 600 exports/$s/$f; echo; done; head -5 corrections/batch-1.csv; sed -n 60,200p ../tools/check_payroll.py

cd /app/data; python3 -V; python3 -c "import zoneinfo;print(zoneinfo.ZoneInfo('Asia/Kathmandu'))"; ls /usr/share/zoneinfo | head -3; for f in $(find exports -type f); do head -c2 $f | xxd -p; done | sort | uniq -c; grep -l '^H' -r exports/kiln | head -0; grep -h '^H' -r exports/kiln | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | awk '{print length($0)}' | sort | uniq -c; grep -rhc schema exports/ridgeline | sort | uniq -c; grep -rh 'Badge\|Zone' exports/harbor-point exports/southbank | sort | uniq -c | head

cd /app && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
s=open('bin/payroll.py').read()
a=s.index('    first = naive.replace(tzinfo=tz, fold=0)')
b=s.index('    return to_epoch(chosen)')
new='''    first = naive.replace(tzinfo=tz, fold=0)
    second = naive.replace(tzinfo=tz, fold=1)
    chosen = first
    if first.utcoffset() > second.utcoffset() and dst is False:
        chosen = second  # repeated time, standard-time occurrence
'''
open('bin/payroll.py','w').write(s[:a]+new+s[b:])
EOF
mkdir -p out && time python3 bin/payroll.py data out/payroll.json && python3 tools/check_payroll.py

cd /app && cat > STATUS.json <<'EOF'
{"status": "success", "summary": "Wrote /app/bin/payroll.py (stdlib only) implementing the documented formats and rules for all nine sites, and saved its output for /app/data to /app/out/payroll.json; tools/check_payroll.py reports every value matching the approved figures."}
EOF
python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('STATUS.json')))"
